INSTITUTIONAL COLLAPSE PSYCHOLOGY (SR‑ICP): A Structural Theory of How Institutions Lose and Attempt to Restore Effective Control Under Drift, Saturation, and Representational Displacement

DESCRIPTION

Institutional Collapse Psychology (SR‑ICP) is a specialized subfield of the SR Institutional Governance Field (SR‑IGF) that explains how institutions can remain formally intact while losing effective control over the environments they are mandated to govern. ICP defines collapse as a persistent divergence between formal authority and effective control, expressed through the Unicode equation:

FECG(d,t) = F(d,t) − E(d,t)

where F is formal authority and E is effective control over the same domain.

The paper introduces a full SR collapse architecture, including:

  • Authority–Control Divergence

  • Institutional Drift

  • Buffer Saturation

  • Representational Displacement

  • Correction Failure

  • Agency Migration

  • Visibility Lag

  • Collapse Boundary Tests

  • Institutional Collapse Ledger

ICP shows how institutions can preserve visible continuity—budgets, buildings, reports, procedures—while losing the ability to perceive, interpret, correct, or influence the conditions central to their mandate. Collapse becomes measurable when correction cycles repeatedly fail, representation mismatches grow, and effective control migrates outward faster than the institution can reconstruct or override.

The architecture is falsifiable, preregisterable, and fully integrated into SR’s governance science.

HOW IT CONTRIBUTES TO SR

1. ICP formalizes collapse as a measurable SR object

ICP introduces the Unicode construct:

FECG = F − E

giving SR a quantitative way to detect when institutions retain authority but lose control.
Linked concept: Authority–Control Divergence

2. ICP provides the institutional mechanism behind Drift Collapse

ICP explains how institutions behave when structural pressure outruns capacity:

  • narrowing interpretation

  • intensifying routine

  • transferring pressure

  • outsourcing cognition

  • compressing representation

  • normalizing crisis

  • losing override capacity

Unicode drift specification:

D(t+1) = D(t) + αM(t) + βVL(t) + γSᵢ(t) − δCCI(t) + ε(t)

Linked concept: Institutional Drift

3. ICP defines Representational Displacement as a cross‑metatheory failure

Institutions govern through representations. ICP shows how representation migrates outward while reconstruction capacity falls.

Unicode displacement index:

RDIₜ = Σ(wₛ·eₛₜ·(1−rₛₜ)) ÷ Σ(wₛ)

Linked concept: Representational Displacement

4. ICP explains institutional behaviour under saturation

Unicode saturation equation:

Sᵢ = Lᵢ ÷ Cᵢᵉᶠᶠ

with:

Cᵢᵉᶠᶠ = Cᵇᵃˢᵉ + B − F

This is the institutional counterpart to SR‑HAT’s human saturation mechanism.
Linked concept: Institutional Saturation

5. ICP connects institutional collapse to Human Agency Transfer

Unicode institutional control share:

ICSₜ = Σ(wₛ·cᵢₛₜ) ÷ Σ(wₛ)

ICP shows how institutions lose control over:

  • evidence selection

  • representation

  • prioritization

  • evaluation

  • execution

while retaining accountability.
Linked concept: Agency Migration

6. ICP provides the governance‑side mechanism for Ultiverse behavioural discontinuity

The Ultiverse predicts:

behavioural discontinuity before institutional discontinuity.

ICP explains why institutions misclassify, respond slowly, govern outdated categories, and lose override capacity.
Linked concept: Behavioural Discontinuity

7. ICP introduces the Institutional Collapse Ledger

This is SR’s first case‑level measurement architecture for collapse regimes. It records:

  • mandate

  • authority

  • effective control

  • representation

  • override capacity

  • correction chain

  • saturation

  • drift velocity

  • migration

  • restoration capacity

CCI = pᴰ × pᴬ × pˣ × pⱽ

Linked concept: Collapse Ledger
